title: Module Assessment: AsyncIO & Concurrency (PY_244 to PY_250)

slides.title: Module 7 Overview
slides.prompt: Assessment covering Event Loops, Async/Await syntax, Tasks, Futures, Gathering Coroutines, and Asynchronous Synchronization primitives.
slides.codeSnippet:
import asyncio

async def main():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Question 1: Event Loop Core Function
slides.prompt: What is the primary role of the AsyncIO Event Loop?
options: To manage and execute asynchronous tasks and handle I/O events cooperatively
To execute multiple CPU-bound loops in parallel across threads
To automatically compile Python bytecode into C code
To replace standard Python garbage collection
slides.correctAnswer: To manage and execute asynchronous tasks and handle I/O events cooperatively

slides.title: Question 2: Async Function Declaration
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to define a coroutine function.

slides.title: Question 3: Pausing Coroutines
slides.prompt: Which keyword suspends execution of the current coroutine until the awaited object yields a result?

slides.title: Question 4: Concurrent Execution with Gather
slides.prompt: Which function runs multiple awaitable objects concurrently and returns their results in order as a list?

slides.title: Question 5: Creating Tasks
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to schedule a coroutine to run on the event loop as a background Task.

slides.title: Question 6: Non-blocking Sleeping
slides.prompt: Why should `asyncio.sleep()` be used instead of `time.sleep()` inside coroutines?
options: time.sleep() blocks the entire event loop, while asyncio.sleep() yields control to other tasks
time.sleep() raises a RuntimeError inside async functions
slides.correctAnswer: time.sleep() blocks the entire event loop, while asyncio.sleep() yields control to other tasks

slides.title: Question 7: Task Cancellation
slides.prompt: What exception is raised inside a Task when its `.cancel()` method is invoked?

slides.title: Question 8: Async Iteration Protocol
slides.prompt: Fill in the magic method that returns an asynchronous iterator object.

slides.title: Question 9: Running Blocking Code in Async
slides.prompt: Which method offloads blocking CPU-bound or synchronous I/O code to a thread pool executor from an event loop?

slides.title: Question 10: Async Context Managers
slides.prompt: Which statement enters an asynchronous context manager?

slides.title: Question 11: Task Timeouts
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to wrap an awaitable and enforce a maximum execution duration (Python 3.11+).

slides.title: Question 12: Asynchronous Queues
slides.prompt: Which queue class from `asyncio` provides thread-safe producer-consumer communication for coroutines?

slides.title: Question 13: Exception Handling in Gather
slides.prompt: What happens if `return_exceptions=True` is passed to `asyncio.gather()` when one task raises an exception?
options: Exceptions are treated as successful results and included in the returned list
The gather function immediately cancels all other tasks and re-raises
It triggers a fatal process crash
slides.correctAnswer: Exceptions are treated as successful results and included in the returned list
